why.title: Ship fires are a different battlefield
why.description: For cruise ships, cargo vessels, offshore platforms, and high-speed craft, fire is the second-greatest threat after sinking. Narrow compartments, vertical passages, enclosed engine rooms, and hot metal structures demand tactics entirely different from land-based building fires.
why.lead: Firefighters often enter at the hottest point and work downward — this reverse-advancement logic only becomes muscle memory through repeated drills in realistic hull structures. Classrooms or ordinary building floors rarely recreate hatches, ship doors, and engine-room routes.
why.body: TZJ maritime training facilities are modeled on real vessels, integrating bridge, engine room, cargo holds, ship doors, and gangways so port fire, maritime rescue, and coastal teams can drill against a repeatable syllabus on land.

props.title: Bridge / wheelhouse
props.desc: Realistic bridge layout with blackout windows for smoke search and command coordination.

props.title: Ship ladders / hatches
props.desc: Vertical deck transitions with steep ladders and hatches for boarding, transfer, and casualty movement.

props.title: Ship doors (multi-dog)
props.desc: Multiple dogged door styles for opening, forcible entry, and advance between compartments.

props.title: Engine-room fire
props.desc: Hot, confined engine-room spaces with flange-fire simulators for attack, cooling, and egress.

props.title: Reconfigurable maze
props.desc: Trackless maze systems that reconfigure inside compartments for low-visibility search and orientation.

props.title: Cargo / storage holds
props.desc: Cargo and storage props with portholes for cargo-fire and confined-space rescue drills.
